creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Four lints the checker already has the information to run. Between them they caught three real bugs in shipped scripts during the review, none of which produced any diagnostic.

**Constant truthiness on always-populated returns.** `cb:8-11` and `linkto:9-13` test `get_path()`'s result for truthiness, meaning "does this exist". Under the current API the map is never empty, so `linkto` always reports "Target already exists." Two latent bugs from one API migration. The general class: any API moving from a nullable or tuple return to an always-populated map silently constant-folds its old callers' conditions. The review calls this the worst failure mode a migration can have, worse than the loud breaks, and its adversary round flagged it as underweighted.

**A function body reading an outer-scope variable instead of its near-miss-named parameter.** `sib:85` returns `p.split("=")`, reading the top-level loop variable `p` from `sib:28` rather than its own `path` parameter. A real bug, in a script with 92 runs.

**A local shadowing a builtin.** Also the cheap half of the `+=` card in p0-tier1.

**Duplicate values in an enum constraint.** `pos:21` declares `enum ["cash","movements","movements","positions"]`.

Two more from the same family if the plumbing is open anyway: an unused variable masking a dropped value (`gkrelay:44-51` builds a body map then posts without it, with a "doesn't quite work for some reason" comment two lines above), and metacharacter-only literal separators like `split(s, ".")`.

Give each rule "since version" metadata. The review's argument for it: version upgrades stop being archaeology and become a checklist.

---

### Orientation
- All four lints live in the static checker, `rts/check`. That placement is what makes them show up in editors too, since `radls` consumes the same package.
- AST-walking lints go in `rts/check/ast_checks.go` and are registered by adding a call inside `RadCheckerImpl.Check()` (`rts/check/check.go:78-107`). Read `addRadOptionNoEffectWarnings` (`rts/check/ast_checks.go:202-231`) as the template: walk, match, append a `Diagnostic` with a code.
- Lints that need the symbol table or types instead use the already-computed `resolved` / `typeInfo` (`rts/check/check.go:88-92`) and surface through `addBindIssues` / `addTypeIssues`.
- `rts` must not import `core`.

### Where to start
Per rule:

- **Constant truthiness on always-populated returns.** The signature in `docs/funcs/get_path.md` confirms the premise: `exists` and `full_path` are non-optional, so the returned map is never empty and truthiness is always true. This is a type-level fact, so it belongs with the type checker (`rts/check/type_check.go`) rather than a raw AST walk - `narrow.go` already reasons about truthiness partitioning (`rts/check/narrow.go:402-470`).
- **Outer-scope read instead of the near-miss-named parameter.** Binder territory. `rts/check/binder.go` already tracks scopes and emits shadowing-family issues - see `ErrHoistedFunctionShadowsArgument` at `rts/check/binder.go:233-234`, and the shadowing comments at `:461`, `:489`, `:576`.
- **Local shadowing a builtin.** Also binder. The registered function names the checker knows about come from `rts/embedded/functions.txt` (generated - see `function-metadata/extract.go`), already used for did-you-mean suggestions.
- **Duplicate values in an enum constraint.** Pure AST. `rl.ArgEnumConstraint` is at `rts/rl/ast_types.go:781-785` with a `Values []string` and its own `Span_`; reach it via `ArgBlock.EnumConstraints` (`rts/rl/ast_types.go:711`). Cheapest of the four - start here.

Codes and docs:
- `rts/rl/errors.go:119-133` is the 4xxxx validation/lint band. Highest in use is `ErrIntLiteralOutOfRange = 40015`, so new codes start at 40016. Numbers are never reused (tombstone rule, `rts/rl/errors.go:6-22`).
- Every new code needs `core/error_docs/<code>.md`; style guide is `core/error_docs/AGENTS.md`. `docs-web/docs/reference/errors.md` is generated from those.

"Since version" metadata is new plumbing, not a field that exists: `Diagnostic` (`rts/check/structs.go:38-47`) carries only `Severity`, `Message`, `Code`, `Suggestion`. Adding it means touching that struct, `diagnosticFromBindIssue` (`rts/check/check.go:167-175`), the renderer loop in the embedded `check` command (`core/embedded/check:25-46`), and the LSP diagnostic mapping in `radls`.

### How to verify
```sh
make build
go test ./rts/check/ -run TestCheckSnapshots -update=lints
go test ./rts/...
go test ./core/testing/ -run TestSnapshots -update=misc/check
make generate && make verify-generated
```
Checker snapshots live in `rts/check/snapshots/` (test `TestCheckSnapshots`, `rts/check/snapshot_test.go:30`). The end-to-end rendered form of `rad check` is snapshotted separately at `core/testing/snapshots/misc/check.snap`. Note `./rts/...` as a whole does not accept the update flags - only packages owning a snapshot suite register them.

### Done when
- Each rule fires on its motivating case and, importantly, does not fire on the legitimate near-misses.
- Each new code has an entry in `rts/rl/errors.go`, a doc at `core/error_docs/<code>.md`, and appears in the regenerated `docs-web/docs/reference/errors.md`.
- Snapshot cases in `rts/check/snapshots/` covering both the positive and the negative for every rule.
- If "since version" ships, it renders in `rad check` output and the schema change is reflected in the LSP path too.

### Watch out for
- Read the `strictOnlyCodes` comment at `rts/check/check.go:139-146` before deciding default severity. RAD30011 was demoted to `--strict`-only precisely because it fired on every fallible builtin and became ~73% of all hints in a real-script sweep. Constant-truthiness has the same shape of risk - if it can't be made precise, ship it behind `--strict` and say so.
- The four rules are independent and land cleanly as separate commits. The enum-duplicate one is a genuinely small AST walk; the constant-truthiness one is the deep type-checker change. Don't let the estimate on the second block the first.
- `c.ast` is nil whenever the file has invalid syntax (`rts/check/check.go:58-65` swallows the converter panic), and `Resolve`/`TypeCheck` are skipped with it (`:88-92`). Every AST-based check must no-op on nil, as the existing ones do.
title: Ship the cheap semantic lints
